video_title: Sam Amick on the Sacramento Kings' growing frustrations & recent roster moves

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Kings' struggles and the viral bickering between LaVine and Sabonis
quotes.excerpt: some of the weird moments that did go viral with LaVine and Sabonis just bickering
quotes.quote: It is crazy how much that one win meant to them. I have been going to these games and feeling the energy in the fan ends. In the San Antonio game, I found myself thinking that you could actually tell these guys are tired of losing. In the first half, I started thinking they were going to take advantage of that opportunity. But then you see some of the similar bright downs that happen almost every time. Then you see some of the weird moments that did go viral with LaVine and Sabonis just bickering about defensive assignments and rebounds and things like that. So it fell apart. They are not in a good place.
quotes.social_post: Sam Amick on the Kings' internal tension: You can see the frustration boiling over, noting the viral moments of LaVine and Sabonis bickering on the court. They are not in a good place right now.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Domantas Sabonis' defensive struggles and the team's frustration
quotes.excerpt: defensively, Domantas Sabonis really struggles to protect the rim. So that is a glaring thing
quotes.quote: Defensively, Domantas Sabonis really struggles to protect the rim. So that is a glaring thing that has been hurting them quite a bit. As we get deeper into the season, you are going to see the human component show itself a little more frequently. When you have guys that have mostly said all the right things, they know they make a bunch of money and that they are lucky to be in the league. These are like the big, big picture rationalizations that you hear from them when they get asked about all the losing. But none of them want to be in this type of a situation. That frustration is going to bear out because the reality is they are not in control of their own futures.
quotes.social_post: Sam Amick highlights the Kings' defensive woes, specifically pointing to Domantas Sabonis struggling to protect the rim as a major factor in the team's ongoing struggles.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Kings' roster moves and the role of Malik Monk and Gabe Vincent
quotes.excerpt: the Malik Monk and Gabe Vincent one, I don't know, it is just a body
quotes.quote: The Malik Monk and Gabe Vincent one, I don't know, it is just a body. If they could find a deal for Malik, they would. Obviously that is his role cuts into Malik's role and they wanted more of a table setter. Gabe is not a prototypical table setter. He can score the ball. I tend to look at Gabe and say for one, certainly it is cool that you have a little bit of a local angle there just with his history in Stockton. But we also forget just in terms of him being a solid NBA player, this guy started for the Heat on their Finals run in 23.
quotes.social_post: On the Kings' roster moves, Sam Amick notes that if the team could find a deal for Malik Monk, they would, while questioning the fit of Gabe Vincent as a table setter for the current rotation.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Unexpected struggles of the Cavaliers and other teams
quotes.excerpt: we did not expect the Cavaliers to be nine and nine
quotes.quote: We did not expect the Cavaliers to be nine and nine. The Magic, back when they traded for Desmond Bane, they were trying to become a contender in the East and they are seven and 10. The Wizards being seven and 12 is a bit of a surprise, but not a shocker. The Raptors with the Kawhi Leonard injury, these are all, most of those teams are pushing their way down to the bottom. And then it obviously just gets uglier from there. The Pacers, injury is a big part of it with Haliburton's situation.
quotes.social_post: Sam Amick surveys the early season landscape, noting the unexpected struggles of teams like the Cavaliers and Magic as the league standings begin to take shape.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Kings' coaching uncertainty and lack of long-term commitment
quotes.excerpt: nobody is saying in no certain terms that he will be the coach until the end
quotes.quote: Admittedly checking on it every game or so, nobody is saying in no certain terms that he will be the coach until the end of the year. So in lieu of that messaging, then obviously part of the job is just to kind of see which way the wind blows. But we are not, to my knowledge, seeing public comments from players that might tilt the scales. And honestly, I am curious your opinion about this. What are your thoughts on the patience level? The energy in the gym doesn't actually seem awful to me, even though the team is awful.
quotes.social_post: Regarding the Kings' coaching situation, Sam Amick reports that there is no definitive word on job security, noting that nobody is saying in no certain terms that the coach will be there until the end of the year.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors' early season struggles and injury issues
quotes.excerpt: they go zero and three to start the year. Then I was at that game down in LA
quotes.quote: They go zero and three to start the year. Then I was at that game down in LA when they lost to the Lakers and looked terrible. Steph actually played obviously, but they had no Podziemski, obviously no Jimmy Butler. Porzingis was out of course. But they get smoked. They look like a terrible team and I am predicting like, oh there is no way this is even a play-in team. But then I tell you what, that eight-game winning streak, I still don't know what to think about because the Yaxel stuff was, it is like was it an aberration? Was it a harbinger of things to come? I don't know. But then when Steph goes down, now they are an even worse version of the team than that zero and three version.
quotes.social_post: Sam Amick reflects on the Warriors' inconsistent start, noting that with Steph Curry sidelined, the team looks like an even worse version of the squad that opened the season 0-3.

quotes.speaker: Sam Amick
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green's contract status and potential for trade
quotes.excerpt: he picked up his player option for this season Draymond did
quotes.quote: He picked up his player option for this season Draymond did and they chose not to extend his contract at all. And even he has been pretty open about what that means. Does it mean the Warriors don't appreciate everything he's done for them over the years? No. Does it mean that he's definitely out? No. But when you have these kinds of conversations, it's the guys with the expiring contracts that are easiest to put into a deal to make the numbers work. And, you know, depending on who the other team is, it's just, you know, he's a guy that A, can still defend at a high level, still play at a high level.
quotes.social_post: Sam Amick discusses Draymond Green's contract status, noting that because he is on an expiring deal, he is the type of player who is easiest to put into a trade to make the numbers work.
